# Notes.ThatVetGuy

> Free academic resources, thoughtfully made for future vets.

Notes.ThatVetGuy (Rx Notes by ThatVetGuy) is a free academic library for BVSc & AH students in India. Site summaries: Dr. Chirag Patidar, BVSc & AH, MVSc. Notes and recommended reading are organised by professional year and subject. Topic notes open on Google Drive or their credited source PDFs and documents; objective and clinical collections open in Telegram. Book recommendations do not imply a downloadable copy is available. Known source credits are preserved; inclusion does not imply authorship or medical review.

Main website: https://thatvetguy.net
Author: Dr. Chirag Patidar
Last source review: 2026-10-26. File access settings can change.

---
Canonical: https://notes.thatvetguy.net/

Reading recommendations. Expand a title for guidance.

A practical starting text for anatomical terminology, organ systems and exam preparation.

Reading recommendation · no linked copy available.

No notes found.

[Request a resource ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/)

Course focus & study tips 

Veterinary Anatomy focuses on relating structure to function across domestic animal species. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Use labelled diagrams to compare the same structure between species, then explain its functional significance.

- Osteology and arthrology
- Myology and visceral anatomy
- Neuroanatomy and sense organs
- Histology and embryology

Use labelled diagrams to compare the same structure between species, then explain its functional significance.

No notes found.

[Request a resource ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/)

Course focus & study tips 

Veterinary Physiology focuses on understanding how healthy animals maintain normal body functions. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Draw a process from stimulus to response before learning the individual hormones, transporters or feedback loops.

- Blood and cardiovascular physiology
- Respiratory and renal physiology
- Digestion and metabolism
- Endocrine and reproductive physiology

Draw a process from stimulus to response before learning the individual hormones, transporters or feedback loops.

Course focus & study tips 

Livestock Production Management focuses on connecting animal husbandry principles with practical farm management. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare management requirements by species, age and production stage, with welfare and daily observation in view.

- Housing and animal handling
- Cattle and buffalo management
- Sheep and goat management
- Poultry production and farm records

Compare management requirements by species, age and production stage, with welfare and daily observation in view.

Course focus & study tips 

Veterinary Biochemistry focuses on linking molecular processes with animal health and nutrition. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Build pathway maps around inputs, outputs and regulation instead of memorising disconnected reaction names.

- Carbohydrate, lipid and protein metabolism
- Enzymes and biological oxidation
- Vitamins and minerals
- Molecular biology and biochemical tests

Build pathway maps around inputs, outputs and regulation instead of memorising disconnected reaction names.

Biochemistry appears in the 1st Year outline PDF; it is grouped in 2nd Year here. Check your university’s syllabus.

Course focus & study tips 

Veterinary Microbiology focuses on distinguishing infectious agents and the host responses they provoke. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare each agent by classification, transmission and laboratory identification while keeping species context clear.

- Bacteriology and mycology
- Veterinary virology
- Immunology
- Microbial genetics and biotechnology

Compare each agent by classification, transmission and laboratory identification while keeping species context clear.

Course focus & study tips 

Veterinary Pathology focuses on recognising mechanisms of disease and the lesions they produce. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Link the underlying mechanism to gross and microscopic changes, then practise describing lesions precisely.

- Cell injury and inflammation
- Circulatory disturbances
- Systemic pathology
- Necropsy and diagnostic sampling

Link the underlying mechanism to gross and microscopic changes, then practise describing lesions precisely.

Course focus & study tips 

Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology focuses on connecting drug action with species, safety and clinical context. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Organise drug classes by mechanism, indications and adverse effects; verify clinical details against a current professional reference.

- General pharmacology and pharmacokinetics
- Systemic pharmacology
- Antimicrobial and antiparasitic agents
- Toxicology and poisoning principles

Organise drug classes by mechanism, indications and adverse effects; verify clinical details against a current professional reference.

Course focus & study tips 

Veterinary Parasitology focuses on understanding parasite life cycles and their significance in animal health. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Sketch life cycles with hosts and infective stages, then connect those stages to diagnosis and prevention.

- Helminthology
- Veterinary protozoology
- Veterinary entomology and acarology
- Parasitological diagnosis and control

Course focus & study tips

This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Course focus & study tips

This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Course focus & study tips 

Veterinary Gynaecology and Obstetrics focuses on understanding reproduction, fertility and obstetrical principles across species. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare reproductive timelines by species, then relate abnormal findings to the relevant stage and clinical history.

- Reproductive cycles and breeding
- Infertility and reproductive disorders
- Pregnancy and parturition
- Obstetrics, andrology and assisted reproduction

Compare reproductive timelines by species, then relate abnormal findings to the relevant stage and clinical history.

Course focus & study tips 

Veterinary Clinical Practices II focuses on integrating supervised clinical learning across the final professional year. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Present cases with a concise history, problem list and reasoned plan, and document what needs further confirmation.

- Clinical examination and diagnostic planning
- Medical and surgical case discussions

# 1st Year Roadmap

Learn the normal. The abnormal can wait one year.

- [1Foundation](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/roadmap/)
- [2Disease & nutrition](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/roadmap/)
- [3Applied study](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/roadmap/)
- [4Clinical](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/)
- [Internship](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/#internship)

MSVE 2016 · Syllabus & outline notes

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

Course-outline note. The uploaded 1st Year outline also includes Biochemistry and prints 21 credits. This guide uses the 18-credit MSVE professional-year distribution; Biochemistry is in 2nd Year here. Check your university's allocation.

## Year at a glance

- 18credits12 theory + 6 practical
- 3core coursesAnatomy · Physiology · LPM
- 50%to passtheory and practical, counted separately
- 210teaching daysminimum; annual exam days excluded

- Use diagrams and specimens alongside theory; practical identification deserves its own revision time.
- Non-credit activities still need a satisfactory grade. Check your college's required programme.

Attendance: 75% minimum in theory and practical separately. 210 teaching days minimum, excluding annual exams.

## Where the credits go

Bigger bar, bigger commitment.

TheoryPractical

Tap a row to find its books and notes.

- [Anatomy4 theory + 3 practical7 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-anatomy/)
- [Physiology4 theory + 1 practical5 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-physiology/)
- [Livestock Production4 theory + 2 practical6 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/livestock-production-management/)

18 credits in total · 12 theory + 6 practical.

## Exam checkpoints

Internal marks are your safety net.

- 1

### Internal 1

By 30% course coverage

40 marks · close the first gaps
- 2

### Internal 2

By 60% course coverage

40 marks · connect the concepts
- 3

### Internal 3

By 90% course coverage

40 marks · revisit weak areas
- 4

### Annual exam

100% of the course

Full course · theory and practical

For theory-bearing subjects: three internals of 40 marks each; the best two assessments count under MSVE 2016. Use your university’s current dates and marking scheme.

## Your subject playbook

Know what to learn. Know how to revise.

1

### Veterinary Anatomy

Focus on Bones and joints; regional anatomy; histology and embryology.

Try this Learn a structure with its location, relations and function. Redraw it, then identify it on a specimen or slide.

A beautiful diagram with no labels is still an expensive doodle.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-anatomy/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-anatomy/#notes)

2

### Veterinary Physiology

Focus on Blood, cardiovascular and respiratory function; digestion; renal, endocrine and reproductive physiology.

Try this Explain each process as a sequence with feedback. Connect the practical observation to the mechanism it demonstrates.

If you cannot explain the feedback loop, rereading the arrow will not help.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-physiology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-physiology/#notes)

3

### Livestock Production Management

Focus on Species-wise husbandry, housing, feeding management, handling and farm records.

Try this Compare species and life stages in a small table. Link each management practice to what you observe on the farm.

Do not leave LPM for the evening before the practical.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/livestock-production-management/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/livestock-production-management/#notes)

## A week that works

Suggested rhythm. Adjust it to your timetable.

- 

### After class

Close the notes and explain one process or redraw one labelled structure. Check what you missed.

- 

### After practicals

Finish observations while you remember the specimen, technique or farm visit.

- 

### At the weekend

Revisit older diagrams and one LPM comparison before planning the next week.

## Small habits, big saves

- Keep one main set of notes per subject; add corrections there instead of starting another notebook.
- Look at past professional papers for format and topic coverage, not a promise of repeated questions.
- Keep attendance and practical records up to date; they are not last-night tasks.

Study advice, not an exam rule. A first-person account by Dr. Bhupender (AIEEA Animal Science 2022 Rank 1) informed the concise-revision and error-review habits; his PG strategy is not a professional-exam blueprint.

## Before the final stretch

- 

### Map the course

Tick off theory units and practical competencies against your university outline.

- 

### Practise the format

Write timed answers with labelled diagrams; rehearse identification and viva explanations.

- 

### Repair weak spots

Use a short list of recurring mistakes, then revisit the original explanation.

Your skeleton has enough bones. Your folder does not need 47 versions.

# 2nd Year Roadmap

Five subjects. Connect the dots, not five new notebooks.

- [1Foundation](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/roadmap/)
- [2Disease & nutrition](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/roadmap/)
- [3Applied study](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/roadmap/)
- [4Clinical](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/)
- [Internship](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/#internship)

MSVE 2016 · Syllabus & outline notes

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

Course-outline note. Biochemistry appears in the uploaded 1st Year outline PDF. The MSVE professional-year distribution used here places it in 2nd Year.

## Year at a glance

- 22credits15 theory + 7 practical
- 5core coursesTheory and practical courses
- 50%to passtheory and practical, counted separately
- 3 × 40internal marksthree scheduled tests; 40 marks each

- Connect Pathology and Microbiology, but keep regular slots for Genetics and Nutrition calculations.
- Finish practical records alongside the laboratory work; explain the observation, not just the result.

Attendance: 75% minimum in theory and practical separately. 210 teaching days minimum, excluding annual exams.

## Where the credits go

Bigger bar, bigger commitment.

TheoryPractical

Tap a row to find its books and notes.

- [Pathology4 theory + 2 practical6 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-pathology/)
- [Microbiology3 theory + 2 practical5 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-microbiology/)
- [Nutrition3 theory + 1 practical4 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-nutrition/)
- [Genetics & Breeding3 theory + 1 practical4 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-genetics-and-breeding/)
- [Biochemistry2 theory + 1 practical3 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-biochemistry/)

22 credits in total · 15 theory + 7 practical.

## Exam checkpoints

Keep the number subjects warm all year.

- 1

### Internal 1

By 30% course coverage

40 marks · close the first gaps
- 2

### Internal 2

By 60% course coverage

40 marks · connect the concepts
- 3

### Internal 3

By 90% course coverage

40 marks · revisit weak areas
- 4

### Annual exam

100% of the course

Full course · theory and practical

For theory-bearing subjects: three internals of 40 marks each; the best two assessments count under MSVE 2016. Use your university’s current dates and marking scheme.

## Your subject playbook

Know what to learn. Know how to revise.

1

### Veterinary Pathology

Focus on General and systemic pathology; oncology; clinical pathology and necropsy.

Try this Link cause, mechanism, gross lesion and microscopic change. Practise describing a lesion before naming a disease.

A disease name is not a lesion description.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-pathology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-pathology/#notes)

2

### Veterinary Microbiology

Focus on Bacteriology, mycology, virology, immunology and microbial biotechnology.

Try this Compare organisms by transmission, pathogenesis and diagnostic approach. Revise laboratory identification with the related theory.

Organism names are not a substitute for understanding the test.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-microbiology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-microbiology/#notes)

3

### Animal Nutrition

Focus on Nutrients, feed evaluation, digestion and species-wise feeding principles.

Try this Work through ration and requirement examples with units shown. Explain the biological assumption behind each calculation.

The calculator cannot rescue the wrong units.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-nutrition/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-nutrition/#notes)

4

### Animal Genetics and Breeding

Focus on Inheritance, population and quantitative genetics; selection and breeding systems.

Try this Write what each symbol means before using a formula. Solve fresh examples and check the interpretation, not only the number.

Memorising the formula is step one, not the whole personality.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-genetics-and-breeding/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-genetics-and-breeding/#notes)

5

### Veterinary Biochemistry

Focus on Biomolecules, enzymes, metabolism, vitamins, minerals and biochemical methods.

Try this Map inputs, outputs and regulation of pathways. Connect biochemical tests to the principle being measured.

Do not turn a pathway into a list of unrelated reaction names.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-biochemistry/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-biochemistry/#notes)

## A week that works

Suggested rhythm. Adjust it to your timetable.

- 

### Pair related topics

Study a pathogen with its lesions and the relevant laboratory method.

- 

### Keep numbers warm

Practise Genetics or Nutrition problems regularly, with working and units.

- 

### Close the loop

Review one lab observation and one older pathway without looking at the answer first.

## Small habits, big saves

- Use comparison tables only when they clarify a genuine distinction; avoid rewriting the whole textbook.
- Record why an answer was wrong: a concept gap, a missed fact, weak recall or an avoidable error.
- Keep the practical method, observation and interpretation together in your revision notes.

Study advice, not an exam rule. A first-person account by Dr. Bhupender (AIEEA Animal Science 2022 Rank 1) informed the concise-revision and error-review habits; his PG strategy is not a professional-exam blueprint.

## Before the final stretch

- 

### Separate the tasks

Make different checklists for descriptive answers, calculations and practical identification.

- 

### Practise mixed work

Alternate a calculation with a lesion or organism explanation to expose weak connections.

- 

### Revisit mistakes

Correct misunderstood concepts before repeatedly attempting the same question.

The syllabus is multiplying. At least your bacteria have an excuse.

# 3rd Year Roadmap

Now the earlier years start asking to be remembered.

- [1Foundation](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/roadmap/)
- [2Disease & nutrition](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/roadmap/)
- [3Applied study](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/roadmap/)
- [4Clinical](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/)
- [Internship](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/#internship)

MSVE 2016 · Syllabus & outline notes

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

## Year at a glance

- 24credits15 theory + 9 practical
- 7core coursesTheory and practical courses
- 50%to passtheory and practical, counted separately
- 3 × 40internal marksthree scheduled tests; 40 marks each

- Link the agent, disease process and prevention or treatment principle across subjects.
- Clinical Practices I and Livestock Farm Practices are practical courses; keep their records and assessment dates visible.

Attendance: 75% minimum in theory and practical separately. 210 teaching days minimum, excluding annual exams.

## Where the credits go

Bigger bar, bigger commitment.

TheoryPractical

Tap a row to find its books and notes.

- [Pharmacology & Toxicology4 theory + 1 practical5 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-pharmacology-and-toxicology/)
- [Parasitology3 theory + 2 practical5 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-parasitology/)
- [Public Health & Epidemiology3 theory + 1 practical4 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-public-health-and-epidemiology/)
- [Extension Education3 theory + 1 practical4 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-and-animal-husbandry-extension-education/)
- [Livestock Products Tech2 theory + 1 practical3 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-products-technology/)
- [Clinical Practices I0 theory + 1 practical1 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-clinical-practices-i/)
- [Livestock Farm Practices0 theory + 2 practical2 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-farm-practices/)

24 credits in total · 15 theory + 9 practical.

## Exam checkpoints

Applied subjects reward practical understanding.

- 1

### Internal 1

By 30% course coverage

40 marks · close the first gaps
- 2

### Internal 2

By 60% course coverage

40 marks · connect the concepts
- 3

### Internal 3

By 90% course coverage

40 marks · revisit weak areas
- 4

### Annual exam

100% of the course

Full course · theory and practical

For theory-bearing subjects: three internals of 40 marks each; the best two assessments count under MSVE 2016. Use your university’s current dates and marking scheme.

Practical-only courses: VCC/LFC assessments follow a separate schedule at 50% and full course completion. Records, observed skills and viva preparation matter.

## Your subject playbook

Know what to learn. Know how to revise.

1

### Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology

Focus on General pharmacology; system-wise drugs; chemotherapy and toxicology.

Try this Organise each class by mechanism, uses, adverse effects and important cautions. Practise unit conversions from worked academic examples.

A brand name is not a mechanism of action.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-pharmacology-and-toxicology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-pharmacology-and-toxicology/#notes)

2

### Veterinary Parasitology

Focus on Helminths, arthropods and protozoa; identification, life cycles and diagnosis.

Try this Draw a life cycle with host, infective stage and diagnostic stage. Link each control principle to the point it interrupts.

Do not mix up the infective stage and the stage you identify.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-parasitology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-parasitology/#notes)

3

### Veterinary Public Health and Epidemiology

Focus on Zoonoses, food and environmental hygiene; epidemiological measures and investigations.

Try this Connect the source, transmission route and prevention. Work through epidemiology measures using the correct denominator.

The denominator is doing more work than the highlighter.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-public-health-and-epidemiology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-public-health-and-epidemiology/#notes)

4

### Veterinary and Animal Husbandry Extension Education

Focus on Communication, extension methods, rural sociology, economics and entrepreneurship.

Try this Apply each method to a real livestock-owner situation. Practise explaining a technical message clearly in everyday language.

A perfectly memorised message still needs someone to understand it.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-and-animal-husbandry-extension-education/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-and-animal-husbandry-extension-education/#notes)

5

### Livestock Products Technology

Focus on Milk, meat and egg processing; product quality, preservation and abattoir practices.

Try this Make process flows with the purpose of each stage. Link a quality test to the property it assesses.

Learn why the process exists, not just the arrows between boxes.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-products-technology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-products-technology/#notes)

6

### Veterinary Clinical Practices I

Focus on Patient handling, clinical examination, case registration and diagnostic orientation.

Try this Observe a structured examination with your supervisor. Record findings, unfamiliar terms and the questions you need to ask.

A case log is more useful before the memory expires.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-clinical-practices-i/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-clinical-practices-i/#notes)

7

### Livestock Farm Practices

Focus on Farm routines, animal records, feeding and management observations.

Try this Keep the day's farm activity and its purpose together. Ask for feedback on handling and record-keeping skills.

Farm records do not become easier when copied from memory in bulk.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-farm-practices/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-farm-practices/#notes)

## A week that works

Suggested rhythm. Adjust it to your timetable.

- 

### Connect three subjects

Use one example to link the disease process, causative agent and drug or prevention principle.

- 

### Make practicals count

Finish the case or farm record on the day and ask about one unclear step.

- 

### Revisit the foundations

Bring back relevant Physiology, Pathology or Microbiology when a new topic depends on it.

## Small habits, big saves

- Compress your own revision material after understanding a topic; a short note cannot replace a missing concept.
- Keep one error list and revisit it before the next practice session.
- Use professional exam papers for your university scheme; PG entrance questions have a different purpose.

Study advice, not an exam rule. A first-person account by Dr. Bhupender (AIEEA Animal Science 2022 Rank 1) informed the concise-revision and error-review habits; his PG strategy is not a professional-exam blueprint.

## Before the final stretch

- 

### Map every course

Include both practical-only courses, not just the five theory subjects.

- 

### Rehearse explanations

Practise a drug-class comparison, a parasite life cycle and an epidemiology problem.

- 

### Check practical readiness

Revisit identification, records and supervised skills as well as written answers.

Everything is connected. Unfortunately, so are your exam dates.

Sources & academic notes 

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

All seven courses are included below. Farm Practices contributes the final 2 practical credits, bringing the year to 24.

- Veterinary Council of India — MSVE Regulations, 2016Gazette, 12 July 2016: regulations 2, 11–13, 15–16; professional-year transcript in Annexure I.
- ICAR–Indian Veterinary Research Institute — Undergraduate ProgrammeSystem of education; professional-year course distribution; examinations.

Assessment coverage is cumulative: the 30%, 60% and 90% milestones are not guaranteed chapter ranges or predicted exam weightage.

Study suggestions are original editorial guidance based on the course topics and a reviewed first-person preparation account. No marks or rank are promised.

Research checked 24 October 2026.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/[BVSc](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/)/[4th Year](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/)/4th Year BVSc & AH Roadmap

# 4th Year Roadmap

From knowing the answer to explaining your next step.

- [1Foundation](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/roadmap/)
- [2Disease & nutrition](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/roadmap/)
- [3Applied study](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/roadmap/)
- [4Clinical](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/)
- [Internship](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/#internship)

MSVE 2016 · Syllabus & outline notes

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

## Year at a glance

- 17credits8 theory + 9 practical
- 4core coursesTheory and practical courses
- 1.5years18 months before the separate internship
- 50%to passtheory and practical, counted separately

- Bring Anatomy, Physiology, Pathology and Pharmacology into case-based reasoning.
- Clinical Practices II is a 0+6 practical course. Follow its clinical assessment and logbook requirements, not the theory-internal template.

Attendance: 75% minimum in theory and practical separately. 315 teaching days minimum, excluding annual exams.

## Where the credits go

Bigger bar, bigger commitment.

TheoryPractical

Tap a row to find its books and notes.

- [Medicine4 theory + 1 practical5 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-medicine/)
- [Surgery & Radiology2 theory + 1 practical3 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-surgery-and-radiology/)
- [Gynaecology & Obstetrics2 theory + 1 practical3 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-gynaecology-and-obstetrics/)
- [Clinical Practices II0 theory + 6 practical6 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-clinical-practices-ii/)

17 credits in total · 8 theory + 9 practical.

## Exam checkpoints

Practise the reasoning, not just the answer.

- 1

### Internal 1

By 30% course coverage

40 marks · close the first gaps
- 2

### Internal 2

By 60% course coverage

40 marks · connect the concepts
- 3

### Internal 3

By 90% course coverage

40 marks · revisit weak areas
- 4

### Annual exam

100% of the course

Full course · theory and practical

For theory-bearing subjects: three internals of 40 marks each; the best two assessments count under MSVE 2016. Use your university’s current dates and marking scheme.

Practical-only courses: VCC/LFC assessments follow a separate schedule at 50% and full course completion. Records, observed skills and viva preparation matter.

## Your subject playbook

Know what to learn. Know how to revise.

1

### Veterinary Medicine

Focus on Systemic and infectious diseases; diagnostic reasoning and preventive medicine.

Try this Present a case as history, findings, problem list and differentials. Explain which test would help distinguish them to your supervisor.

A list of diseases is not yet a differential diagnosis.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-medicine/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-medicine/#notes)

2

### Veterinary Surgery and Radiology

Focus on Surgical principles, anaesthesiology, imaging and regional surgery.

Try this Learn the indication and anatomical basis of a procedure with its preparation and aftercare. Practise permitted skills under supervision.

Knowing the instrument's name is the opening scene, not the whole surgery.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-surgery-and-radiology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-surgery-and-radiology/#notes)

3

### Veterinary Gynaecology and Obstetrics

Focus on Reproduction, obstetrics, infertility and reproductive management.

Try this Link normal reproductive physiology to clinical findings. Compare species and practise structured case explanations.

Species differences have entered the chat.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-gynaecology-and-obstetrics/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-gynaecology-and-obstetrics/#notes)

4

### Veterinary Clinical Practices II

Focus on Clinical rotations, case work, diagnostics and supervised clinical competencies.

Try this Keep a de-identified case log: what you observed, your reasoning, feedback and what you will review next.

The logbook is evidence of learning, not a scrapbook of signatures.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-clinical-practices-ii/#books)

## A week that works

Suggested rhythm. Adjust it to your timetable.

- 

### Before a posting

Review the examination approach and one relevant foundation topic.

- 

### After a case

Write a de-identified summary, check your reasoning and ask your supervisor for feedback.

- 

### Before the next week

Revisit unresolved questions and practical skills without letting written revision disappear.

## Small habits, big saves

- Explain why you chose an investigation or management principle; memorised lists alone do not show reasoning.
- Keep patient identifiers out of personal study notes and discuss cases within your institution's rules.
- Use current, species-appropriate references and supervisor guidance; a revision sheet is not a prescription.

Study advice, not an exam rule. A first-person account by Dr. Bhupender (AIEEA Animal Science 2022 Rank 1) informed the concise-revision and error-review habits; his PG strategy is not a professional-exam blueprint.

## Before the final stretch

- 

### Connect theory to cases

Practise concise problem lists, differentials and reasons for investigations.

- 

### Prepare both formats

Rehearse written answers and the practical examination or viva separately.

- 

### Prepare for internship

Check completion of credits, records and university instructions for rotating postings.

The patient did not read your predicted questions.

## Next stop: internship

After passing the fourth professional and completing the required credits, the MSVE 2016 programme includes a separate compulsory 12-month rotating internship.

Follow your university’s posting schedule, supervision, logbook and completion requirements. Clinical Practices II is part of the fourth professional; it is not the internship.

Sources & academic notes 

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

The fourth professional spans 18 months under MSVE 2016, followed by a separate compulsory 12-month rotating internship.

- Veterinary Council of India — MSVE Regulations, 2016Gazette, 12 July 2016: regulations 2, 11–13, 15–16; professional-year transcript in Annexure I.
- ICAR–Indian Veterinary Research Institute — Undergraduate ProgrammeSystem of education; professional-year course distribution; examinations.

Assessment coverage is cumulative: the 30%, 60% and 90% milestones are not guaranteed chapter ranges or predicted exam weightage.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/Tips & Tools for Vet Study

# Tips & Tools for Vet Study

Explore practical AI study guidance, useful free apps and everyday study tools for veterinary students. Use the guides to organise reading, references and presentations while checking veterinary information against trusted sources.

[Tools](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/study-tools/#tools)[Tips](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/study-tools/#tips)

## Use of AI for Vet Study

- 

### Start with your outline

Ask AI to organise a topic list or suggest a presentation structure. Compare the result with your syllabus and original notes.

- 

### Check before you learn

Verify veterinary facts and citations. A fluent answer can still be wrong; AI output is not a prescribing reference.

- 

### Make the explanation yours

Explain the topic without looking at the answer. Rewrite it in your own words and credit your sources.

## Useful Free Apps

- 

### Zotero

Keep reading references together. Check each citation against its original source.

- 

### LibreOffice

Prepare notes, tables and presentations. Keep an editable copy as well as a PDF.

- 

### Your PDF reader

Use bookmarks, annotations and text search. Keep essential reading in a clearly named offline folder.

## Useful Study Tools

- 

### A document scanner

Scan only material you have permission to copy. Check every page for legibility before sharing.

- 

### A simple folder system

Try Year / Subject / Notes or Books. A useful filename saves a surprising amount of searching.

- 

### A reference checklist

Record the author, edition, species and date where relevant. A saved file still needs context.

## Year Roadmaps

[1st Year Roadmap](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/roadmap/)[2nd Year Roadmap](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/roadmap/)[3rd Year Roadmap](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/roadmap/)[4th Year Roadmap](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/)

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/About Notes.ThatVetGuy

# About Notes.ThatVetGuy

Notes.ThatVetGuy is a free academic library for BVSc & AH students. Find notes, books and practical material by year, with study guides to help you choose what to read next.

## A useful place to start.

Pick your professional year, find a subject and get to the reading. Notes.ThatVetGuy brings notes, books and practical material together for veterinary students.

## People behind the pages

Site guidance and summaries are by Dr. Chirag Patidar, BVSc & AH, MVSc. Linked materials retain their original authorship. Inclusion does not imply medical review or ownership.

## Help the next student

A missing topic, a broken file or a credit that needs correcting: tell us so the library can get better.

[Request or report a resource ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/)

## Questions, answered

Where do resources open?

Topic-wise notes open on Google Drive. Objective notes, question banks, drug references and handbooks open in Telegram; some collections require access. Recommended books do not always have a linked copy. Original authors retain credit.

Does the year grouping match my syllabus?

Year grouping may vary by university. Check your syllabus before planning revision.

Page updated: 2026-10-20. Sources last reviewed: 2026-10-26; external file availability can change.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/Can’t find what you need?

# Can’t find what you need?

Request a veterinary note, book, PYQ or useful study resource, or report a link that needs attention. Include the subject, year and source so the library can be improved for other veterinary students.

↳ Can't find it? Ask. The library has an excellent memory.

## Tell us what would help.

Include the topic, subject, year and edition if relevant.

File ID, if reporting a file

[Email your request ](mailto:contact@thatvetguy.net?subject=Resource%20request)

You can also copy contact@thatvetguy.net into your email app.

## Contact

Send your question to contact@thatvetguy.net.

## Contribute

Send the title, subject and original source credit. Share only material you have permission to contribute.

## Report an error / takedown

Include the file ID or page URL, the issue and your contact details. For a takedown request, explain your connection to the material.

## Questions, answered

How do I report a broken link?

Email contact@thatvetguy.net with the page URL and resource name. The visible email address can be copied if your email application does not open.

Can I contribute a resource?

Send the original source, title and subject to contact@thatvetguy.net. Share material you have permission to contribute.

# Drug Index Collection

Veterinary drug indexes, a drug handbook, a wall reference and vaccination schedules in one collection. Open a resource in Telegram and check its edition before clinical use.

For study, not prescribing. Verify the species, dose and current clinical guidance before treating a patient.

## Drug references & schedules

#1

### VENDEX: The Fundamental Veterinary Drug Index

A veterinary drug-index reference to consult alongside current product information.

[Open Book: VENDEX: The Fundamental Veterinary Drug Index](https://t.me/c/4430259212/3)

#2

### Veterinary Drug Index by NAVSARI

A veterinary drug-reference collection labelled NAVSARI.

NAVSARI

[Open Book: Veterinary Drug Index by NAVSARI](https://t.me/c/4430259212/4)

#3

### Plumb’s Veterinary Drug Handbook

A drug-handbook reference. Check the edition and species-specific guidance before use.

[Open Book: Plumb’s Veterinary Drug Handbook](https://t.me/c/4430259212/5)

#4

### Drug Dose — Wall Reference

A printable quick-reference sheet; verify every dose against current clinical guidance.

[Open Book: Drug Dose — Wall Reference](https://t.me/c/4430259212/7)

#5

### Vaccination Schedule of All Animals

A vaccination-schedule reference to compare with species, local guidance and product labels.

[Open Book: Vaccination Schedule of All Animals](https://t.me/c/4430259212/6)

These links open a private Telegram collection. You need access to that collection to view its posts.
